method.method_draft: Use a visual steepness comparison. First read the graph as a distance-versus-time line graph with time in hours on the horizontal axis and distance in miles on the vertical axis. Look at each one-hour interval: 0–1, 1–2, 2–3, and so on. Since all intervals are one hour long, the largest average speed corresponds to the segment with the greatest upward slope. Visually, the segment from hour 1 to hour 2 rises much more steeply than any other one-hour segment, so the largest average speed occurs during the second hour, 1–2.

method.method_draft: Make an approximate table of cumulative distances at the integer-hour marks from the graph, then compare one-hour distance gains. Read approximate values such as distance at 0 hours about 0 miles, at 1 hour about 350–400 miles, at 2 hours about 900 miles, at 3 hours about 1050 miles, at 8 hours about 1550 miles, at 9 hours about 1750 miles, and at 12 hours about 1850–1900 miles. Compute or estimate the increases for one-hour intervals: from 0 to 1 is about 350–400 miles, from 1 to 2 is about 500+ miles, from 2 to 3 is much smaller, from 3 to 8 is about 100 miles per hour, from 8 to 9 is about 200 miles, and from 9 onward is smaller. The greatest one-hour increase is from 1 to 2 hours, so the answer is the second hour.
